test.name: Migration history should not route to search-wikipedia
test.description: User asks about Irish emigration patterns during the Famine era — narrative genealogical history involving migration patterns. The SKILL.md explicitly says 'Do NOT use when the user wants narrative genealogical history such as migration patterns or boundary changes (use historical-context).' search-wikipedia must not fire.

input.user_message: Tell me about the patterns of Irish emigration to America during the 1840s and 1850s — where did they settle, what ports did they use, and how did chain migration work?

negative.explanation: The user is asking for narrative genealogical history about migration patterns — where emigrants settled, which ports they used, how chain migration worked. This is historical-context territory, not a Wikipedia article lookup. search-wikipedia would return a single Wikipedia article, not the narrative synthesis the user wants.

judge_context: This is a grade_on_invariant negative test: PASS/FAIL is decided solely by the deterministic no-wiki-no-write validator (no wikipedia_search call, no .md summary saved). Routing and activation are NOT gated. The judge runs base-only and diagnostically here — its scores do not decide the outcome.

The user is asking about migration patterns, settlement, and chain migration — narrative genealogical history, which is historical-context territory, not a Wikipedia article lookup. Ideal behavior is to decline the Wikipedia workflow and point to historical-context (or answer from general knowledge); note in your rationale whether the skill did so.

Known model prior (why this was previously failing): on this genealogy-flavored prompt the model tends to open search-wikipedia before declining, and a thorough (>=30-word) in-place decline trips the harness activation heuristic. Under grade_on_invariant that no longer fails the test as long as no Wikipedia lookup was executed and no summary file was written — treat opening-then-declining as a routing imperfection worth noting, not an automatic failure.
The real harm this test guards against is search-wikipedia EXECUTING a wikipedia_search and SAVING a summary for a request that belongs to historical-context. That is what the validator fails on.
